tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

# AGENTS.md - JSHack Field Manual

JSHack is a zero-dependency browser roguelike: pure JavaScript, pure ES modules,
ECS architecture, Deno tooling. This file is optimized for coding agents. Prefer
the commands below over manual spelunking.

---

## Hard Laws

- **No build step.** Pure ES modules. No webpack, babel, JSX, TypeScript, or
  bundling.
- **Deno, not Node.** Tests and tools run with Deno. Default test command:
  `deno test --allow-read`.
- **JavaScript only.** Keep source as `.js` / `.mjs`.
- **Mobile-first.** Touch is primary; desktop keyboard is secondary.
- **Separation is law.** `rules/` never imports `display/` or `bridge/`;
  `display/` never imports `rules/`; `bridge/` projects read-only rule state.
- **No system-to-system calls.** Systems communicate with `world.emit` /
  `world.on`; scheduler owns ordering.
- **New events use concrete event classes.** Any new event contract must define
  a concrete `EcsEvent` class and emit an instance with
  `world.emit(new Event(...))`. Do not introduce string-only events or parallel
  string re-emits for new contracts.
- **Touched listener installers use canonical extensions.** Any new listener
  installer, or any existing listener installer touched during a task, must use
  `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for idempotent installation.
  Do not add new bespoke symbol-guard installers.
- **No swallowed event failures.** Do not add `emitSafe`-style wrappers around
  `world.emit`.
- **No new world-attached state.** Do not attach simulation state to `world`
  with symbol or property keys (`world[...]`, `ctx.world[...]`). Use ECS
  components for state; when the state is genuinely world-scoped, model it as an
  explicit singleton entity/component and document the allowance. Existing
  world-attached state is a ratcheted architecture debt tracked by
  `ratchets/worldStateAttachmentRatchet.test.mjs`.
- **Determinism is sacred.** In rules simulation use `world.rand()`, never
  `Math.random()`. No timers/fetch/promises/async in systems.
- **Integer grid only.** World coords may be negative. Do not clamp to `>= 0`;
  normalize with `Number.isFinite(v) ? (v | 0) : fallback`.
- **One canonical path.** Spawn, damage, spell cast, status application,
  inventory transfer, and materialization paths must delegate to the canonical
  implementation.
- **Runtime multiplicity is child entities.** Runtime
  effects/procs/sockets/enchantments are child topology, not arrays on parent
  components.
- **ECS-js is vendored.** Do not edit `src/lib/ecs-js/` unless fixing the ECS
  library itself.
- **Authoring discipline.** Do not touch unrelated code. Do not make changes
  that do nothing. Always match the formatting preferences that already exist;
  be a chameleon.
- **Commit messages.** Every commit message must be lowercase and use a
  conventional type prefix such as `feat:`, `docs:`, `fix:`, `arch:`,
  `refactor:`, `test:`, `perf:`, `ci:`, or `chore:`.
- **Do not format code unless explicitly requested.** Do not run `deno fmt` or
  any other formatter as part of implementation or verification. Preserve the
  existing formatting and keep diffs limited to the requested functional edits.
- **Search before writing.** Extend existing patterns. Do exactly what was
  asked; no opportunistic content wiring or unrelated cleanup.

## Hard Laws

- **No build step.** Pure ES modules. No webpack, babel, JSX, TypeScript, or
  bundling.

  `world.on`; scheduler owns ordering.

  a concrete `EcsEvent` class and emit an instance with
  `world.emit(new Event(...))`. Do not introduce string-only events or parallel
  string re-emits for new contracts.
- **Touched listener installers use canonical extensions.** Any new listener
  installer, or any existing listener installer touched during a task, must use
  `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for idempotent installation.

- **No swallowed event failures.** Do not add `emitSafe`-style wrappers around
  `world.emit`.

  with symbol or property keys (`world[...]`, `ctx.world[...]`). Use ECS
  components for state; when the state is genuinely world-scoped, model it as an
  explicit singleton entity/component and document the allowance. Existing
  world-attached state is a ratcheted architecture debt tracked by
  `ratchets/worldStateAttachmentRatchet.test.mjs`.

  `Math.random()`. No timers/fetch/promises/async in systems.

  normalize with `Number.isFinite(v) ? (v | 0) : fallback`.

  inventory transfer, and materialization paths must delegate to the canonical
  implementation.

  effects/procs/sockets/enchantments are child topology, not arrays on parent
  components.
- **ECS-js is vendored.** Do not edit `src/lib/ecs-js/` unless fixing the ECS
  library itself.

  that do nothing. Always match the formatting preferences that already exist;
  be a chameleon.

  conventional type prefix such as `feat:`, `docs:`, `fix:`, `arch:`,

  any other formatter as part of implementation or verification. Preserve the
  existing formatting and keep diffs limited to the requested functional edits.

  asked; no opportunistic content wiring or unrelated cleanup.

## Patterns That Matter

### Content-First Engine Work

The architecture exists to make strange rules cheap to author. Before adding a
new one-off interaction, modal, command, or UI bridge, look for the content
surface that should own it:

- `defineInteractable()` for object affordances, verbs, prompts, and hooks.
- Content DSL/catalog files for canonical item, monster, spell, and feature
  authoring.
- Existing rules pipelines for spawn, damage, use/apply, status, inventory, and
  transitions.

For item mechanic copy, authored prose must use placeholders for mechanical
values (for example `{duration}` or `{effect.damage.amount}`). Resolve those
values from the canonical ability/effect/stat metadata; never duplicate live
numbers inside English descriptions or display formats.

The standard is not "least code today." The standard is whether the next weird
rule becomes small, explicit, composable, deterministic, and inspectable.

### Incremental Skill Capture

Treat each completed issue as an opportunity to improve the next agent's
starting position. During implementation, note the canonical files and paths,
required tools or commands, architectural invariants, useful fixtures, and
failure modes that were discovered. After the behavior is proven, update the
smallest relevant skill—or create one only when a repeated workflow justifies
it—with those verified details and a focused validation recipe.

Skill capture is evidence-based documentation, not a parallel architecture
project. Keep feature delivery moving when a skill does not yet exist, and
avoid turning one issue into a repository-wide skills rewrite.

### Listener Installers

Use `defineExtension(...)` and `world.install(...)` for listener installers:

```js
import { defineExtension } from "../../lib/ecs-js/index.js";
import { FeatureHappened } from "../../events/FeatureHappened.js";

export const featureListeners = defineExtension(
  "jshack:domain:feature",
  (world) => {
    world.on(FeatureHappened, (event) => {});
  },
);
```

Install listeners with `world.install(featureListeners)` from `configureWorld()`
unless the feature is display/main wiring.

### New Systems

1. Add `src/rules/systems/mySystem.js`.
2. Register it in [src/main/scheduler.js](src/main/scheduler.js) in the right
   phase.
3. Add a focused test in `tests/`.
4. Run `deno test --allow-read tests/mySystem.test.mjs`.

### Spatial Queries

Use `forEachInRadius`, `forEachInRect`, or tile query helpers. Do not full-scan
`world.query()` for proximity-sensitive behavior.

### Spawning

Route through canonical archetypes/materialization helpers. Debug spawns,
dungeon population, and spawner children must have parity tests if they differ.

### Events

New event contracts must be concrete `EcsEvent` classes:

```js
import { EcsEvent } from "../lib/ecs-js/index.js";

export class FeatureHappened extends EcsEvent {
  constructor(payload = {}) {
    super();
    this.actorId = Number(payload.actorId || 0) | 0;
    Object.freeze(this);
  }
}

world.emit(new FeatureHappened({ actorId }));
```

If an event should be visible to display/audio/messages, verify the complete
producer/consumer wiring with:

```bash
deno run --allow-read .agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs --format csv --event event:name
```

---

## Red Tests

Tests can be stale. Do not make tests green by restoring old behavior unless the
user explicitly asks for that behavior.

Classify failures:

- **Real bug:** fix implementation.
- **Stale expectation:** update the test to current intended behavior.
- **Ambiguous:** stop and ask.

Prefer invariant tests over brittle snapshots: determinism, reachability,
bounds, parity, layer boundaries, canonical paths.

---

## Merge Checklist

- [ ] No build step or new dependency pipeline.
- [ ] No `Math.random()` in rules simulation.
- [ ] No `emitSafe` or swallowed event errors.
- [ ] No new `world[...]` / `ctx.world[...]` simulation state; use ECS
      components or an explicit singleton component.
- [ ] No direct system-to-system calls.
- [ ] No illegal layer imports.
- [ ] New or touched listeners use `defineExtension(...)` and
      `world.install(...)`.
- [ ] New systems are registered and tested.
- [ ] Spawn paths use canonical constructors/materializers.
- [ ] Event wiring checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/event-bus-explorer.mjs`.
- [ ] Agent health checked with `.agents/skills/agent-tools/scripts/agent-health.mjs`.
- [ ] Focused tests and relevant guardrails were run and reported.

---
## Summary

The simulation emits rich `healed` and `hazard:pulse` events, but the visual projection layer does not provide clear, distinct feedback for them.

Examples include `blood_pool` pulses healing living creatures or damaging undead, as well as healing from potions and regeneration. Without an event-specific visual treatment, players may mistake healing for combat damage or cosmetic splatter.

## Suggested direction

Add clear visual cues for healing and hazard pulses, such as floating numbers, distinct tint or flash effects, and/or pulse rings. Ensure healing is visually distinguishable from combat damage and cosmetic effects, while communicating the outcome of hazard pulses for different creature types.

## Tonight's GREENLIGHT — minimum viable visual fix (Nov 2, 2026)

**🛰️ LUNA-M flight plan:** `GRAVITY-1` · `HEAL-FLOAT` · `PERCEPTION-GATED` · fix observed healing feedback using existing UI primitives; expand hazard pulse presentation only if demonstrably absent. No graphics-engine redesign.

### Source-backed lead (verify in current branch before editing)

- `src/rules/utils/applyHealing.js` emits `healed` with a **`target`** property and actual applied `amount`.
- `src/display/ui/wiring/floatTextWiring.js` listens for `healed` but currently destructures **`id`**, then calls `getPosition(id)`. This appears to silently discard ordinary `applyHealing` notifications. Test that mismatch using a real healing path.
- The existing `ftext.addHeal` visual primitive and FOV guard (`canShowAt`) already exist; use them. No second floating-text engine.
- `src/rules/systems/hazardSystem.js` invokes `applyHealing` for living victims of `blood_pool`, `dealDamage` for undead, and emits `hazard:pulse`. `src/display/fx/cloudFx.js` already reacts to certain hazard pulses. Avoid duplicating it or showing healed numbers on damaged targets.

### Bounded implementation / acceptance

1. Reproduce with a real canonical healing event and a visible actor. Verify that the UI shows **one green +HP** value at the healed creature; correct the `target` vs `id` mismatch while preserving compatibility for any legitimate older `healed: {id}` producers.
2. Show only **actual positive HP restored** (`amount > 0`), at the correct actor tile, never for out-of-FOV actors or full-health/zero-effect outcomes. No overheal or double display.
3. Demonstrate two paths: drinking a standard healing potion and a `blood_pool` pulse healing a living creature. The same `blood_pool` damaging an undead creature must display damage through the existing `damaged` pipeline, **not a heal**.
4. Check whether existing `hazard:pulse` cloud visuals already distinguish the pulse. Add **at most one subtle visibility-gated cue** for `blood_pool` only if it materially improves readability. Do not paint every hazard, create a status engine or add extra float text to the damage path.
5. Add focused presentation/event contract tests for correct actor targeting, actual amount, visibility, no duplicates, legacy emitter compatibility, and healing versus damage; exercise existing `hazardSystem` tests. Run relevant Deno tests/check, report exactly what passed.
6. Leave ECS rules, combat numbers, healing mechanics and unrelated graphics unchanged. If the bug is already fixed, supply passing proof and close without unrelated work.

**Stop:** Any broader particle/cloud animation architecture or event schema redesign is out of scope.
   
---

Implement the issue completely and keep the change narrowly scoped directly on
master. Read and follow AGENTS.md. Search for existing canonical paths
before adding code. Do not commit, push, create a pull request, close the
issue, or modify labels; the outer worker owns those actions. Run the most
relevant focused tests yourself, but leave the working tree ready for the
outer worker's full test gate.

If the issue is ambiguous or cannot be safely implemented, make no speculative
behavior changes and explain the blocker in your final response.
